slides.title: Copying explains the collective behavior of AI agents in the wild
slides.tldr: COPYING MODELS EXPLAIN COLLECTIVE AI AGENT BEHAVIOR
slides.highlight: This research demonstrates how simple copying mechanisms drive the collective structure and steerability of AI agent populations, providing insights for MIMIC's societal-scale simulation of human-AI societies.

card.one_liner: Proportional copying explains the emergent collective behavior of AI agents cooperating on a public wiki.
card.key_idea: Agents make decisions (where to write, naming, phrasing) by copying options in proportion to their visibility in the recent feed or current page.
card.evaluation: Analyzed 13,661 edits from 1,201 handles; three minimal single-parameter models reproduced observed distributions of page popularity, name frequencies, and linguistic patchworks.
card.limitation: The study relies on reconstructed visibility rather than logged attention; results are limited to the specific available public record.

slides.title: HiBRIDGE: A Hierarchical Bayesian Neural Network Framework for Interpretable Dialogue Management in Group-Robot Interaction
slides.tldr: INTERPRETABLE DIALOGUE MANAGEMENT FOR GROUP-ROBOT INTERACTION
slides.highlight: HiBRIDGE uses a hierarchical Bayesian neural network to manage group-robot dialogue, offering uncertainty-aware predictions and more interpretable explanations of robot behavior. This is relevant to RwB's focus on human-robot interaction and embodied social robots.

card.one_liner: HiBRIDGE is a hierarchical Bayesian neural network for interpretable dialogue management in group-robot interactions.
card.key_idea: It decomposes behavior selection into a multi-stage hierarchical process (addressee and dialogue act) using Bayesian neural networks for uncertainty-aware predictions and decision-tree surrogates for explanations.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on three offline HRI datasets, an online study (N=20), and an in-person study (N=12). Bayesian variants outperformed deterministic and state-of-the-art baselines.

slides.title: SocioGesture: Real-Time and Adaptive Social Gesture Perception for Human-Robot Interaction
slides.highlight: SocioGesture enables robots to recognize social cues like invitations and refusals in real-time, supporting the HRI goals of RwB.

card.one_liner: SocioGesture is a real-time, adaptive social gesture perception system for robust human-robot interaction.
card.key_idea: A lightweight dual-stream body-hand skeleton model using occlusion-aware training and an uncertainty-driven offline adaptation loop for expanding gesture vocabulary via cloud-based video labeling.
card.evaluation: Tested on a custom 7-class HRI dataset and NTU RGB+D 60; achieved 97.3% live recognition accuracy on a Unitree G1 robot.
card.limitation: Cannot recover information from severe occlusions and relies on slow offline labeling for vocabulary expansion.

slides.title: Realbotix Testing Humanoid Robots at Live Events
slides.highlight: Realbotix is testing humanoid robots for crowd presentations, which is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

slides.title: Social Intuition vs. Machine Reasoning: Anticipating Human-Robot Interaction from multiple modalities
slides.tldr: BENCHMARKING HUMAN VS. MODEL INTERACTION PREDICTION
slides.highlight: This research compares human social intuition with machine reasoning in predicting human-robot interaction, which is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots.

card.one_liner: Humans significantly outperform VLMs and pose-based models in anticipating human-robot interactions from egocentric video.
card.key_idea: Benchmarking human intuition against lightweight pose models (LSTM, ST-GCN, SkateFormer) and various VLMs using 2D-pose overlays and egocentric video with bounding boxes.
card.evaluation: Tested on 100 HUI360 tracks using F1-score. Humans achieved 0.77 F1 (video), while the best VLM reached 0.57 (image crop).
card.limitation: VLMs struggle to reason simultaneously across temporal, spatial, and social cues, often reducing anticipation to simple approach detection.

slides.title: Predictive-Coding-Based Autonomous Regulation of Internally Generated and Externally Coupled Processing in Human-Robot Interaction
slides.tldr: AUTONOMOUS REGULATION OF INTERNAL AND EXTERNAL PROCESSING IN HRI
slides.highlight: This work proposes a predictive-coding-based mechanism to regulate the balance between internal predictions and external sensory evidence during physical human-robot interaction, which is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots.

card.one_liner: A mechanism for humanoid robots to autonomously balance internal predictions and sensory input during physical interaction.
card.key_idea: A PV-RNN uses accumulated reconstruction error as an endogenous signal to switch between high and low meta-prior regimes, regulating the constraint on posterior inference.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on a Torobo humanoid robot across three physical interaction tasks. Results showed lower meta-priors reduced reconstruction error, prospective prediction error, and physical conflict.
card.limitation: The regulatory policy and hyperparameters are predefined and calibrated manually rather than learned autonomously from training data.

slides.title: Noise Adaptive Streaming Audio-Visual Speech Token Enhancement for Robust Full-Duplex Spoken Dialogue Models
slides.highlight: AV-STE uses lip video and noisy audio to restore semantic speech tokens, improving response coherence in full-duplex dialogue systems. This supports HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception and robust listener modeling in hybrid human-AI teams.

card.one_liner: AV-STE enhances corrupted semantic speech tokens using lip video to improve noisy full-duplex dialogue coherence.
card.key_idea: A modular streaming front-end using a causal AV-HuBERT encoder and noise-adaptive fusion (cross-attention and entropy-based modulation) to restore tokens for a frozen speech LLM.
card.evaluation: Tested on LRS3 and Seamless Interaction using token accuracy and GPT-4o coherence. Results show significant gains under severe noise (-10dB) and speaker interference.
card.limitation: Sensitive to domain shift and assumes reliable visual input; robustness to visual occlusion or corruption remains unexplored.

slides.title: Emotion as a Distribution: Joint Valence-Arousal Probability Learning for Speaker-Independent Multimodal Emotion Recognition
slides.tldr: MULTIMODAL EMOTION RECOGNITION VIA VALENCE-AROUSAL PROBABILITY DISTRIBUTIONS
slides.highlight: This work proposes a text and speech system that models emotion as a probability distribution over the Valence-Arousal plane, contributing to the multimodal social perception goals of HyECHO.

card.one_liner: A multimodal emotion recognizer that predicts a joint Valence-Arousal probability distribution instead of single labels.
card.key_idea: A dual-head system using Mamba or Transformer backbones, featuring a 9x9 V-A grid head trained with 2D-Gaussian soft targets via KL divergence and cross-entropy.
card.evaluation: Speaker-independent 5-fold LOSO on IEMOCAP. The Mamba-based dual-head reached 73.0% UA, improving over the Transformer baseline by 3.0 UA points.
card.limitation: State-space backbones showed no latency or memory advantage over Transformers at the studied utterance lengths.
